correctness.rationale: For the specified 0<ℓ<1 left branch and arbitrary real r,d right branch, define u=d−ℓr and n=2k+1. Axis return after RL is B(x)=1+ℓ−ux and after RLL is C(x)=1+ℓ+ℓ²−ℓux, so the full word has nonzero multiplier −ℓu^n. Necessary strict LL visit sign B(x₀)<0 yields u^n(u−ℓ)>1+ℓ and hence u>u_k>1; hyperbolic attraction enforces ℓu^n<1. For sufficiency, at u=u_k the distinguished LL is at the switching border, while every other R-input is >0; a small increase u>u_k and sufficiently negative r yields correct strict itinerary, and d=ℓr+u preserves it. Its primitive length is 4k+3 because the LL pair is unique. Window nonempty iff ℓ^(−1/n)>2ℓ+ℓ²; all k iff ℓ≤sqrt(2)−1, otherwise sharp strict logarithmic cutoff. Implicit log expansion gives widths order 1/n or 1/n² on boundary. Independently constructed exact rational strict attracting seven-cycle example and verified branch signs and multiplier.
